key_insight: STAR-XPC uses a Set Transformer to predict X-ray transmission through polymer composites in milliseconds with high agreement to Monte Carlo simulations.
engineering_relevance: The model could accelerate radiation-shielding material screening by reducing reliance on computationally expensive transport simulations.
method: Represent up to 11 molecular constituents using ChemBERTa embeddings and mass fractions.
Combine unordered constituent sets with four bulk physical descriptors in a permutation-invariant Set Transformer.
Train on transmission ratios generated by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy simulation pipeline.
evidence_signal: On 4,697 simulated configurations, leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation achieved R² = 0.9988, MSE = (1.12 ± 0.56) × 10⁻⁴, and median absolute percentage error of 1.15%.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-based; performance beyond the studied polyethylene-based composites, four tube voltages spanning 30–120 kV, and 0.15–2.5 mm thicknesses remains unestablished.
paper_title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
